correctness.rationale: The distorted SIR field sums identically to zero, so applying the all-ones covector to the published hybrid equation gives the exact mass law Mdot=lambda*1^T f_NN. Applying the same covector to the published residual target gives the derivative of the preprocessed observed total. The exact parameter-bias residual is the difference of two SIR fields and is therefore zero-sum. The matrix P=I-(1/3)11^T is the orthogonal projector onto the zero-sum plane; its Pythagorean decomposition proves that projection cannot increase Euclidean error relative to any exact zero-sum residual. These steps require no statistical approximation or unverified numerical claim.

value.rationale: The source explicitly motivates SIR as structurally different from Lotka–Volterra because of conservation, while its optimized hybrid solutions use a large neural contribution. The exact drift law shows which part of that structural information is lost. More importantly, the proposed projection is not an arbitrary regularizer: in the paper's controlled parameter-bias setting the true residual is provably zero-sum, so projection guarantees conservation and can only reduce or preserve pointwise Euclidean error to the residual the network is intended to learn. This makes the result a motivated structural correction rather than a cosmetic constraint.
